**Review: search ad**

**Claims check**

| Claim | Status |
|---|---|
| "Monthly loose leaf tea" | Product fact, fine |
| "If your box isn't right, we'll make it right" | **Unsupported** |
| "Free UK delivery on orders over £25" | Allowlisted |

**Problem**
- "If your box isn't right, we'll make it right" is a satisfaction guarantee. The brand policy has no refund, replacement or remedy promise. The only subscription commitment it backs is that subscribers can pause or cancel any time. The line also promises an outcome ("make it right") that nobody has defined. Ad platforms and UK consumer-advertising rules treat vague guarantees like this as risky when the terms aren't stated.
- **Compliant replacement:** "Pause or cancel any time." This is allowlisted and says something concrete about the subscription.

**Other notes**
- Slop check: no banned words or structural violations. The opening is a plain product fact.
- Landing page: the ad should only make claims the landing page also makes. Check that the page shows the free delivery threshold and the pause/cancel terms.
- Length: the description is about 106 characters. If this is a Google RSA description (90-character limit), it is too long, and the replacement above brings it under. I wasn't given a limit, so confirm the one for your platform.

**Suggested version**
Headline: Tea Subscription UK
Description: Monthly loose leaf tea. Pause or cancel any time. Free UK delivery on orders over £25.

Do not publish as written.
